The Full Claude Ladder: When to Use Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus for Coding

description:
We ran 18 real isolated Claude Code benchmarks across all 3 tiers of Claude 5.5 (Haiku $1.54 vs Sonnet $12.22 vs Opus $29.94).

Is Claude Opus 5.5 really worth paying 20x more than Haiku 5.5 or 2.5x more than Sonnet 5.5? We ran 18 real isolated one-shot benchmarks in Claude Code CLI across 6 extreme physics, WebGL2, and CPU emulation challenges. Opus 5.5 swept the first three physics and multi-pass GPU simulations (3-0), but Haiku 5.5 stunned in Round 4 by building a 61 FPS 3D Acid Techno Studio for $0.21 vs Opus's $5.00, and Sonnet 5.5 won Rounds 5 and 6—doubling Opus's FPS in the WebGL2 Path Tracer (29 vs 15 FPS) and booting live Pong on a curved CRT CHIP-8 console while Opus ($6.93) left its initial ROM at 0 bytes.

DEMOS AND CODE
Play all 18 real interactive demos from Episode 04: https://labs.mixiuh.online
Exact prompts and API cost telemetry at Mixiuh Labs: https://labs.mixiuh.online

02:14 Challenge 2: 100K-Agent GPU Physarum Bio-Network
03:03 Challenge 3: Structural Bridge Live Fracture
03:53 Challenge 4: 3D Acid Techno Studio TB-303 + TR-909
04:48 Challenge 5: WebGL2 BVH Path Tracer & Denoiser
05:35 Challenge 6: Retro CHIP-8 Console & Assembler
06:34 Final verdict: when to use Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus
07:24 Golden rule for choosing Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus

TOOLS
- Voice: Voicefy, cloned voice running locally on Mac (narrated in English).
- Editing and captions: Reelfy + Mixiuh Labs Studio (4K60 pipeline).
- Music: original procedural chiptune generated by code.
- Stack: claude --model haiku/sonnet/opus --effort high (18 isolated runs).

The narration uses my own cloned voice with Voicefy (runs locally).
